text:
If you’re heading onto Lake Champlain, don’t: a Lake Wind Advisory is up, with south winds building to 30 knots and waves rising to 2 to 4 feet. Burlington is still clear and mild at midday, around 72, but the quiet won’t last. Showers should move in after 1, with a high near 74, then steadier rain tonight and a chance for thunder from roughly 8pm through the overnight hours. Expect a half-inch or more of rain, with gusty south winds continuing.

Thursday looks like the reset, with any leftover shower or rumble ending early, then a mostly sunny afternoon near 79. The models are split on how warm and showery it gets, but the forecast leans dry after daybreak. Keep outdoor plans close to town today, skip the lake, and wait for Thursday’s improving skies.

week.blurb: Cloudy, with rain after lunch and a stormy night, high 74, rain odds 90%.
Mostly sunny Thursday, high 79, though early showers are possible and the wetter models argue for an umbrella.
Sunny and seasonably cool Friday, with a high near 72 and a clear, comfortable night.
Bright and mild Saturday, sunny with a high near 77, ideal for outdoor plans.
Partly sunny Sunday, warmer at 81, with showers possible from morning onward, odds around 40%.
Partly sunny Monday, high 75, with only a slight shower chance and a cooler northwest breeze.
Partly sunny but unsettled Tuesday, high near 80, with showers and nighttime thunderstorms possible as south winds gust.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Happy Wednesday! Our Wednesday morning starts off mainly dry but cloudy. We will hang onto the cloud cover through this morning ahead of rain showers that start to make their arrival by this afternoon and evening. Rain could be steadier in nature through this evening and into the night, with the chance for a few isolated rumbles of thunder. High temperatures for the day are cooler as a result of the clouds and showers, with most only in the upper 60s to lower 70s this afternoon. Rain starts to taper by daybreak Thursday morning. Ultimately, I think most places will receive between 0.5″ and 1″ of new rain. Overnight lows are in the low to mid-60s for most places.
